question: Which of the following events is a consequence of atmospheric refraction?

options.text: Curved mirrors to form enlarged image of an object

solution:
The correct answer is __**Advance sunrise and delayed sunset**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Atmospheric Refraction and Sunrise/Sunset:**

 
• Atmospheric refraction is the bending of light as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The atmosphere's density increases as you get closer to the Earth's surface.
 
• This varying density causes light to bend as it travels through the atmosphere.
 
• During sunrise and sunset, sunlight has to travel through a greater portion of the atmosphere.
 
• As the sunlight enters the atmosphere at a shallow angle, it is refracted, or bent.
 
• This bending causes the apparent position of the sun to be slightly higher than its actual position.
 
• As a result, we see the sun before it has physically risen above the horizon (advance sunrise).
 
• Similarly, we continue to see the sun for a short time after it has physically set below the horizon (delayed sunset).
 
• This effect extends the duration of daylight by a few minutes each morning and evening.
 
• The amount of refraction depends on the temperature and density of the air.
 
• Refraction is more pronounced near the horizon because light travels through a denser layer of air.
 
• The phenomenon is also responsible for the oval shape of the sun near the horizon.
 
• Atmospheric refraction also causes the twinkling of stars.
 
• The bending of light is a continuous process as the atmosphere's density changes.
 
• The refractive index of air increases with its density.
 
• The refraction of light is a consequence of the change in the speed of light in different mediums.
 
• The effect is most easily seen when looking at objects very close to the horizon.
 
• The amount of advance sunrise and delayed sunset varies depending on the latitude and time of year.
 
• Atmospheric refraction is a common optical phenomenon.
 
• The effect is most noticable when the sun is very close to the horizon.
 
• The atmosphere acts like a series of prisms bending the light.
 
• The effect of atmospheric refraction is a daily occurrence.
